t: Count Number of Ways to Place Houses
o: Each side of the street is an independent length-n binary string with no two adjacent 1s. If one side has f(n) valid arrangements, the two sides together give f(n)². f is the Fibonacci recurrence: f(1)=2 (empty or house), f(2)=3, f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2) (plot n empty → f(n-1) ways; house at n → plot n-1 empty → f(n-2) ways). Check: n=1 → 2²=4 ✓; n=2 → 3²=9 ✓.
k: The two sides are independent, so the answer is f(n)² where f counts no-adjacent-houses arrangements on one side.
f satisfies the Fibonacci recurrence f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2) with f(1)=2, f(2)=3.
All arithmetic mod 1e9+7; square at the end.

a.i: Iterate the recurrence for one side, then square the result modulo 1e9+7. Multiplication of two residues < 1e9+7 fits in 64-bit / safe doubles in JS.

w: The insight to state out loud is independence of the two sides — many people try a joint 4-state DP over both sides, which also works (states: neither/one/other/both house at current plot) but is unnecessary. Pitfalls: squaring before reducing is fine, but reduce after squaring; in JS use BigInt for the final square to avoid precision loss. Follow-up: closed-form via fast matrix exponentiation for n up to 1e18.
